name: Acute Flaccid Myelitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: CDC Diagnostic Criteria for Acute Flaccid Myelitis

criteria.description: Acute onset of flaccid limb weakness
MRI showing spinal cord lesions largely restricted to gray matter
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses such as transverse myelitis, Guillain-Barré syndrome, or poliomyelitis
CSF pleocytosis or elevated protein supportive but not required

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Acute flaccid limb weakness plus MRI showing spinal cord gray matter lesions and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by MRI and CSF findings; viral etiology often suspected but not always confirmed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Spinal cord gray matter lesions on MRI
searchTerms: spinal cord damage in gray matter
gray matter spots on spine MRI
lesions in spinal cord gray area

common.symptomName: Cranial nerve dysfunction (e.g., facial weakness, dysphagia)
searchTerms: nerve problems in face or swallowing
difficulty swallowing due to nerve issues

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected limbs
Respiratory muscle weakness requiring ventilatory support
Preceding viral prodrome (fever, respiratory illness, or gastrointestinal symptoms)

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction (e.g., bladder or bowel dysfunction)

searchTerms: pain in affected arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Paralysis extending to respiratory muscles without ventilatory support
searchTerms: loss of muscle control including breathing

laboratory: CSF pleocytosis with mild lymphocytic predominance
imaging: MRI showing spinal cord lesions predominantly in gray matter of anterior horns
other: Viral PCR from respiratory or stool samples may detect enteroviruses (e.g., EV-D68)

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
MRI lesions involving both gray and white matter
More prominent sensory and autonomic involvement
History of poliovirus exposure or incomplete vaccination
Similar anterior horn cell involvement but epidemiologically rare

redFlags: Rapid progression of limb weakness over hours to days
Loss of deep tendon reflexes in affected limbs
references: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Acute Flaccid Myelitis (AFM). CDC.gov
Hixon AM, et al. Acute Flaccid Myelitis: Epidemiology, Clinical Features, and Diagnosis. Neurol Clin. 2020
Messacar K, et al. Acute Flaccid Myelitis: A Clinical Review of US Cases 2012-2015. Lancet Neurol. 2016
